clue.text: South American woman in borders of Benin

indicators.note: the woman's name sits inside the other letters, as the clue says she is in them
the borders of a word are its outside letters, its first and last

parts.note: Olivia is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Bolivian woman crosses into the West African state of Benin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woman' tempts as the definition, but the woman is only a name placed in the frame; 'South American' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bolivian is a native of Bolivia, a country of South America.

clue.text: Resonant sound of TV equipment —- it sometimes accompanies 19

definitions.meaning: a deep resonant noise, as of a distant gun
the long pole that holds a microphone over a scene being filmed
19 is BABY, and the baby ... is a well-known phrase for a surge in births

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions, the last pointing at the answer to 19 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a deep echoing noise, a microphone pole in broadcasting, and a sudden surge, as in births.

clue.text: Fire on bird crossing East Beds town

indicators.note: the phrase for igniting reaches across, holding the compass letter inside it

parts.note: to fire something on is to light it on, as a gas burner
E is the compass abbreviation for East
a buzzard is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: Someone sets fire to a bird flying across eastern Bedfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county; LEIGHTON BUZZARD is a market town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leighton Buzzard is a town in Bedfordshire, which is abbreviated Beds.

clue.text: Respect archdeacon bishop's left to upbraid

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: to have left is to have gone away, so the bishop's letter departs from the word for scold

parts.note: to upbraid is to berate, to scold
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An archdeacon is told off once the bishop has gone home.
explanation.walkthrough: Ven, for Venerable, is the formal title of an archdeacon in the Church of England; 'left' signals the bishop departing.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate someone is to respect them deeply, a close synonym.

clue.text: Radical completely taking in a southern state

indicators.note: the word for wholly takes in, or holds, the state's abbreviation

parts.note: all, as in all gone, means completely
KY is the abbreviation for Kentucky, a southern US state

explanation.surface: A political radical takes over a whole Southern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' looks political, but in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkyl group is a chemical radical derived from an alkane, so this is the chemistry sense.

clue.text: Art work university exhibited in southern gallery

indicators.note: the university's letter is shown inside the gallery, as a work is exhibited in one

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A university's artwork goes on show in a gallery in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery; S before it makes STATE, and U goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a work of art.

clue.text: Get on, struggling with posh language

indicators.note: a struggling phrase is in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the classic label for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: Getting on in society while struggling with posh speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges GETON into TONGE; U for posh is the old upper-class label.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language, as in mother tongue.

clue.text: Another Bronte novel — not a bloke in it, naturally

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are arranged afresh
not means without, so the letter A is dropped from the man

parts.note: a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: A further novel by a Bronte sister, with no man in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' drops A from MAN, leaving MN, which goes 'in' with ANOTHER BRONTE; 'novel' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something to the manner born means doing it naturally, as if born to it: an idiom.

clue.text: It polishes unknown soldiers up before pivoting manoeuvre

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British Army corps
Y is a mathematical unknown
a wheel is a turning drill movement about a pivot

explanation.surface: Soldiers carry out a drill in which they wheel about.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a British Army corps of engineers; 'up' turns it in this down clue, and 'before' sets the first part ahead of the drill movement.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery wheel is a grinding wheel coated with abrasive, used for polishing metal.

clue.text: Unidentified writer accepts advice on hard church music

indicators.note: the anonymous writer takes in, or accepts, the other letters

parts.note: anon, short for anonymous, signs work by an unknown author
a tip is a piece of advice
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An anonymous writer takes advice on difficult church music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' signals the anonymous writer containing the rest; 'on' is a link word, and H for hard comes from pencil grading.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiphon is a chant sung in alternate parts in church services.

clue.text: The sort of paper whose content may make us weep!

definitions.text: The sort of paper whose content may make us weep!

parts.words: The sort of paper whose content may make us weep!
parts.note: a thin translucent paper, read jokingly as the outer layer of a bulb that brings tears when cut

explanation.definitionFit: Onionskin is a very thin glossy paper, named after the papery layer of the vegetable.

clue.text: In autumn it requires a fertiliser

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In autumn the garden needs some fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across autumN IT REquires.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre, potassium nitrate, is used as a fertiliser.

clue.text: Time to leave table for tea

indicators.note: the time letter has to leave the word, so it is taken out

parts.note: a chart is a table of data

explanation.surface: It is time to get up from the table for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T from CHART leaves the answer; char is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Char is an informal British word for tea, from the Chinese.

clue.text: Slow-moving island river captured by Dutch painter

indicators.note: the island and river are held inside the painter's name

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A sluggish island river painted by a Dutch master.
explanation.walkthrough: Lely was a Dutch-born painter at the court of Charles II; the Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried, slow-moving.

clue.text: What Macavity could be, having taking ways?

definitions.text: What Macavity could be, having taking ways?

parts.words: What Macavity could be, having taking ways?
parts.note: Macavity is T S Eliot's criminal cat, and taking ways read literally are thieving habits

explanation.walkthrough: Macavity is the Mystery Cat of T S Eliot's Old Possum's poems, a master criminal; taking ways usually means charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat burglar is a thief who climbs into buildings, and Macavity is literally a feline thief.

clue.text: Address to person not present that should be in St Paul's?

definitions.meaning: in rhetoric, a speech turning to address someone absent

definitions.text: that should be in St Paul's?
definitions.meaning: the punctuation mark that belongs in the possessive Paul's

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, punning sense: St Paul's the cathedral needs the mark in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a rhetorical address to someone absent and the punctuation mark showing possession.

clue.text: Dismissed Tory without qualifications

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
the Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A Tory is thrown out with no qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without qualifications' suggests lacking diplomas; here it means unreservedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely, with no reservations or qualifying conditions.

clue.text: Try to crash party

definitions.meaning: to have a ... is to have a try

explanation.surface: Attempting to gatecrash a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings of one word, with 'to' as link; 'crash party' tempts as gatecrash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bash means an attempt, a heavy blow, and a lively party.

clue.text: Hazardous setting for King Edward's court

indicators.note: the risky word forms a setting around the royal letters, as a mount holds a jewel

parts.note: chancy means risky, hazardous
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A dangerous place for King Edward to hold court.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Latin Edwardus Rex; Chancery is a division of the English High Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is the Lord Chancellor's court, a division of the High Court of Justice.

clue.text: Bunting seaman secured in past?

indicators.note: the sailor is held fast inside the word for gone by

parts.note: by can mean past, as in walking by
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Bunting, the flags a sailor once fastened aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' suggests flags or a bird, but it is the nursery rhyme's Baby Bunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunting is an old term of endearment for a baby, as in the rhyme Bye Baby Bunting.

clue.text: Unexpected gen on these prehistoric pillars

indicators.note: the unexpected arrangement means these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Surprising information about these ancient standing stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' rearranges GEN ON THESE; 'gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the famous prehistoric monument of standing stones in Wiltshire.

clue.text: Writer from old Republican source

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A writer drawing on an old Republican source.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was an English novelist and essayist, author of Animal Farm.

clue.text: Bird that's never settled by Santa Claus?

definitions.text: Bird that's never settled by Santa Claus?

parts.words: Bird that's never settled by Santa Claus?
parts.note: a seabird, read as an invoice for shaving blades that the bearded Father Christmas would never pay

explanation.walkthrough: Santa has a full beard, so he never buys shaving gear; a settled bill is one paid.
explanation.definitionFit: The razorbill is a black and white seabird of the auk family.

clue.text: Dipper quietly leaving for lake

indicators.note: the quiet letter leaves, so it is removed from the constellation

parts.note: the Big Dipper is the American name for the Plough
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A diving bird quietly leaves for a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipper' suggests the bird, but is the star group the British call the Plough; lough is Irish for lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lough is the Irish word for a lake or sea inlet, like Scottish loch.

clue.text: Bug found in new chest

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, as the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: An insect turns up in a new chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' as a noun suggests an insect; as a verb it means annoy, and to nark is British slang for irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark someone is to annoy them, so it is a slang synonym of bug.

clue.text: Reportedly Tamworth's accommodation is an eyesore

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: the Tamworth is a breed of pig, which lives in a sty

explanation.surface: Housing in the town of Tamworth is said to be an eyesore.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a town but also a British breed of pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, so literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Green light taken by those on the way out

definitions.text: taken by those on the way out
definitions.meaning: time off, taken by staff going away on holiday or departing

explanation.definitionFit: Leave means both permission and a period of absence from work.

clue.text: River snake aboard extremely hot vessel

indicators.note: the river and snake come aboard, inside the outer letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England
a boa is a constricting snake

explanation.surface: A snake from the river climbs aboard a boat in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes only the ends of hot; 'aboard' puts the river and snake inside, as passengers on a craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a boat fitted out as a home, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Screen mystery

definitions.meaning: a coarse sieve for sifting soil or gravel

explanation.definitionFit: Riddle means both a large sieve and a puzzling question.

clue.text: Native American female entertaining longing to enter church

indicators.note: the combination goes into the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the female holds the longing inside, as a host entertains

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A Native American woman with a longing to go into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'entertaining' puts the longing inside the female bird, then 'to enter' sends that inside the church letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.
